cells.content:
Performance Driven
Employees are encouraged to see failure as an opportunity to learn.

Clear Vision
Everyone is aligned on the same mission.

Embraces Failure
The best culture is driven by performance.

Values Your Time
No pointless meetings or unnecessary overhead.

Shows Empathy
Treats everyone with respect and empathy.

Adapts to Change
Embraces change and adapts quickly.

Open Communication
Communication is two-way and clear across hierarchy levels.

Corrects Bad Behaviour
Bad behaviour is not tolerated and is corrected quickly.

Empowers Hard Work
Hard work is consistently rewarded.

Accepts Disagreement
Healthy debate is understood as critical for success.

Value Driven
Values are acted upon, not replaced by perks like bean bags or pizza Fridays.

Encourages Diversity
Looks for diversity of thoughts and perspectives.

Proactive Culture
Employees take initiative and are encouraged to act.

Empowers Employees
People are trusted to make decisions and own their work.

Proven Track Record
The company has a history of delivering on its promises.

Competitive Salary
Compensation is fair and transparent.

Amazing Company Culture
The workplace is fun, unique, and genuinely enjoyable.

Lots of Perks and Benefits
Genuine benefits — not just a coffee machine.

Mentorship Program
New hires are paired with experienced colleagues.

Transparent Promotion Path
People know how growth and promotion decisions work.

Real Work-Life Balance
Time away from work is genuinely respected.

Clear Budgets and Tools
People have what they need to do good work.

Remote-Friendly
Flexible location is a real policy, not a bait-and-switch.

Internal Mobility
People grow into new roles inside the company, not just out.

Learning Budget
Annual budget for courses, conferences, and books.

Clear Hiring Process
Timelines, steps, and expectations are communicated upfront.
Dodging salary questions
"We are a family"
Unpaid overtime
High turnover
Badmouthing ex-staff
Mandatory pizza parties instead of raises
Salary is not listed in the job post
No transparent promotion path
Time off is discouraged
Poor work-life balance
Company flaws cannot be discussed openly

"Rockstar" wanted
Expects one person to do the work of three.

"Thick skin" required
Criticism is frequent; feedback is not constructive.

Unpaid on-call work
You're available 24/7 but only paid 9-to-5.

Social media presence required
Your personal brand is now the company's marketing.

Mandatory unpaid trial project
Work for free to prove you deserve a paid job.

Equity instead of salary
"The startup equity will be worth millions" — it won't.

"Growth opportunities" = more work
No raise, but here's extra responsibility.

"Ninja" / "Guru" / "Wizard"
Overused titles masking unrealistic expectations.

"Urgently hiring"
Constant urgency; planning is an afterthought.

No psychological safety
Mistakes are punished, not learned from.

"Young and dynamic" code
Age discrimination disguised as culture fit.

Micromanagement disguised as transparency
Every keystroke is tracked and reported.

No sick leave policy
You're expected to work from your deathbed.

Multiple rounds of unpaid interviews
5+ rounds before a decision — respect is absent.

Non-compete clause
You can't leave without losing your career for 2 years.

"Fast-paced environment"
Exciting for some, chaotic for others — depends on the team.

"Wear many hats"
Growth opportunity or scope creep? It depends on boundaries.

"Work hard, play hard"
Fun culture or an excuse for long hours?

"Hit the ground running"
Exciting challenge or zero onboarding?

"Self-starter" needed
Autonomy or abandonment? Depends on support.

"Startup culture"
Scrappy innovation or chaotic disorganisation?

Flexible working hours
Freedom to manage your time — or always-on expectations?

Flat hierarchy
Close to leadership or missing mentorship structure?

"Competitive environment"
Drives excellence or breeds internal rivalry?

"Sense of humour" required
Fun workplace or avoiding serious conversations?

Mandatory team events
Bonding opportunity or unpaid social overtime?

Relaxed dress code
Comfort or lack of professional standards?
